tooltip_popover.title: Repeated Doubling and Exponential Notation
tooltip_popover.content: Multiplicative growth multiplies quantities repeatedly by a constant factor. In exponential expression a^n, 'a' represents the base and 'n' represents the exponent/power.
tooltip_popover.example: Magical Pond Lotus Problem: Lotuses double daily and cover pond on Day 30 -> Pond was half covered on Day 29.

children.name: 2.2 Laws of Exponents and Negative Powers

tooltip_popover.title: 2.2 Laws of Exponents and Negative Powers
Fundamental Laws of Exponents
tooltip_popover.content: Product Law: x^a * x^b = x^(a + b) Quotient Law: x^a / x^b = x^(a - b) Power of a Power Law: (x^a)^b = x^(a * b) Zero Exponent Law: x^0 = 1 for any non-zero x (derived from x^a / x^a = x^(a-a) = 1). Negative Exponent Law: x^(-n) = 1 / (x^n)

tooltip_popover.title: Scientific Notation and Practical Applications
tooltip_popover.content: Powers of 10 enable compact representation of vast and tiny quantities. Scientific notation represents numbers as m * 10^n where 1 <= m < 10.
tooltip_popover.example: Bacteria growth doubling every 20 mins: 100 bacteria after 2 hours (6 doubling periods) = 100 * 2^6 = 6400.
